intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

selected_hotel.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group sessions here, combining gentle Hatha or Vinyasa flow with breathtaking natural views. A deeply restorative experience that blends movement with Bali's spiritual energy.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful and accessible surf spots. Local instructors provide boards and guidance for a 90-minute session. Afterward, relax on the beach and watch the legendary Bali sunset paint the sky in vivid oranges and pinks.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-renowned wellness culture with a multi-class pass at The Yoga Barn in Ubud. Choose from daily classes including Kundalini, Yin, Ashtanga, and meditation. The lush jungle setting, community atmosphere, and variety of skilled teachers make this a highlight for any yoga-focused traveller visiting for 13 days.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Snorkeling & Crystal Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Explore the calm, crystal-clear waters of Nusa Dua and nearby Crystal Bay on a guided snorkeling day trip. Discover vibrant coral reefs, tropical fish, and sea turtles in one of Bali's most pristine coastal areas. Equipment rental and a local boat guide are included, making this an affordable and unforgettable beach adventure.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Ubud Market Tour
experiences.description: Start the morning with a guided walk through the vibrant Ubud Traditional Market, selecting fresh local ingredients with your chef. Then head to a traditional family compound to learn how to prepare authentic Balinese dishes such as Nasi Goreng, Satay Lilit, and Lawar. A hands-on cultural and culinary experience that connects you deeply with local life.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot as flight lands at 1 PM
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at airport, clear customs, exchange currency at airport money changer for fair rates. Take a pre-booked airport taxi or Grab app ride (~IDR 150,000–200,000) to Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along the famous Campuhan Ridge Walk trail — a free, scenic 2 km walk through lush green hillside and rice paddies, perfect for stretching legs after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ubud's Jalan Raya Ubud main street on foot. Visit a local warung (small family restaurant) for your first authentic Balinese meal. Wander around the area near Pura Gunung Lebah temple at the confluence of two rivers — beautiful and free to admire from outside.

meals.breakfast: Skip / grab a light snack at the airport before landing
meals.lunch: Eat at the airport or grab a quick bite near the hotel upon arrival — try a local mini-mart snack pack (IDR 20,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka or a local warung near Ubud center — nasi campur or mie goreng for IDR 25,000–45,000

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is a travel/arrival day. Keep it relaxed. The Campuhan Ridge Walk is free and accessible directly from the hotel — ideal for a gentle first afternoon. Exchange cash at the airport or a reputable money changer in Ubud (avoid hotels for exchange). Grab app works well in Bali for affordable rides.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise walk on the Campuhan Ridge Walk — the trail starts just steps from the hotel. The golden morning light over the jungle and rice terraces is stunning and completely free. Return for a light breakfast before heading out for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud (entry ~IDR 80,000). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ancient temples and interacting with the resident macaques. Afterward, browse the Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for affordable handmade crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs — great for bargaining.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or a nearby venue (tickets ~IDR 100,000–150,000). This mesmerizing cultural show is one of Bali's highlights. Grab dinner at a warung on the walk back.

meals.breakfast: Bubur ayam (rice porridge) or nasi goreng at the hotel or a nearby warung — IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Warung inside or near the Monkey Forest — nasi campur or gado-gado for IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Warung Teges or any local warung near Ubud center — mie goreng or sate lilit for IDR 25,000–45,000

day_by_day.notes: The Campuhan Ridge Walk is best experienced at sunrise or early morning before it gets warm. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. At the Monkey Forest, keep bags zipped and remove sunglasses/hats as monkeys may grab them. Bargain respectfully at the Art Market — start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning yoga class in Ubud — Yoga Barn (IDR 120,000–150,000 per drop-in class) or look for free/donation-based community classes posted on local notice boards. Ubud is Bali's yoga capital with dozens of studios. After class, enjoy a healthy smoothie bowl at a budget café nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (IDR 50,000–80,000/day from local shops near the hotel) and cycle to Tegallalang Rice Terraces (~8 km north of Ubud). Admission is free though a small donation (~IDR 10,000–20,000) is appreciated. Enjoy the iconic UNESCO-listed stepped rice paddies and take photos. Explore the surrounding area on your bike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud by bike or local bemo (minibus). Visit Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — free to view from outside, beautiful architecture. Stroll Monkey Forest Road for budget shopping and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or acai bowl at a budget café near Yoga Barn — IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Pack a snack or eat at a wayside warung near Tegallalang — nasi bungkus (wrapped rice) for IDR 15,000–25,000
meals.dinner: Warung Ibu Oka or Warung Sopa near Ubud center — hearty local meal for IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes in advance during peak season as popular studios fill up. Bicycle rental shops are easy to find near the hotel. The road to Tegallalang has some uphill sections — the ride back is mostly downhill and enjoyable. Bring sunscreen and a water bottle. July is dry season so conditions will be excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tirta Empul Temple (~12 km from Ubud, shared minivan/bemo ~IDR 30,000–50,000 or rent a scooter IDR 70,000–100,000/day). Witness or participate in the sacred purification ritual bathing in the holy spring pools (entry IDR 50,000, sarong rental included). Arrive before 9 AM to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Kintamani and Mount Batur viewpoint (~30 km from Ubud). Enjoy panoramic views of the active volcano and crater lake Batur from the rim (free viewpoint). Have lunch at a warung with a volcano view. Return to Ubud by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel. Optional: join a sunset meditation or yin yoga session at a local studio. Take an evening walk along the Campuhan Ridge Walk as the sun sets over the jungle — magical and free.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or a nearby warung before departing — nasi goreng IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Warung at Kintamani with volcano views — set lunch menu IDR 50,000–80,000 (some restaurants charge a 'view fee' — negotiate or find a local warung)
meals.dinner: Cook-your-own or eat light at a local warung near Campuhan — soup or satay for IDR 25,000–40,000

day_by_day.notes: Renting a scooter gives maximum flexibility for this day trip but requires an international driving permit and confidence on Balinese roads. Alternatively, join a shared day-tour from Ubud (IDR 150,000–250,000 including transport and guide) which is still budget-friendly. At Tirta Empul, dress modestly — sarong and sash are provided.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or stretching session — check Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive studio for budget drop-in classes. Alternatively, do a free self-guided yoga session on the Campuhan Ridge Walk at sunrise using a travel mat. Afterward, visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum (~IDR 80,000 entry) — a unique museum inside the home of eccentric Spanish-Balinese artist Don Antonio Blanco, very close to the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Penestanan village (15–20 min walk from Campuhan) — a charming artists' village with rice fields, local painters' studios, and quiet lanes. Many studios allow free browsing. Visit a traditional silver or wood carving workshop to watch artisans at work (free). Explore the surrounding rice paddy paths on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud for the weekly Ubud Night Market (if scheduled) or browse local food stalls along Jalan Dewi Sita. Try various Balinese street foods — sate, pisang goreng (fried banana), jajan pasar (traditional sweets).

meals.breakfast: Jamu (traditional herbal drink) and toast at a local café — IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Warung in Penestanan village — simple home-cooked nasi campur IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Street food at Ubud Night Market or food stalls — budget IDR 30,000–60,000 for a full spread of snacks and mains

day_by_day.notes: The Blanco Museum is a short walk from the hotel — very convenient. Penestanan is a hidden gem that most tourists miss. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the village lanes are narrow and sometimes uneven. The night market is a great place to try many different local foods at very low prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the coast — take a tourist shuttle bus or Grab to Seminyak or Canggu (~1.5 hrs, IDR 50,000–100,000). Arrive at the beach by mid-morning. Enjoy the famous black-sand beach at Batu Bolong (Canggu) — free entry. Swim, sunbathe, and watch surfers. Canggu has a laid-back, bohemian vibe perfect for budget travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Canggu's beach clubs from the outside (entry fees can be high — enjoy the beach for free instead). Visit Echo Beach or Pererenan Beach for quieter spots. Browse the local surf shops and boutiques along Jalan Batu Bolong. Rent a surfboard for a beginner lesson if interested (IDR 100,000–150,000/hour with instructor).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Canggu sunset from the beach — one of Bali's best. Grab dinner at a budget warung in Canggu before taking a shuttle back to Ubud. The last shuttle typically departs around 7–8 PM.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before departure from hotel — fruit and tea IDR 15,000–25,000
meals.lunch: Warung on Canggu beach — nasi goreng or fish and chips (local style) IDR 35,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Budget warung in Canggu before heading back — babi guling or mie goreng IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the shuttle bus the day before from agencies near the hotel (Perama or similar). Canggu is very popular in July — the beach will be lively. The sea conditions in July are generally good for swimming on the west coast. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a towel, and a change of clothes. Avoid expensive beach clubs — the public beach is equally beautiful and free.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in or do gentle yoga/meditation at the hotel or on the Campuhan Ridge Walk. Visit the nearby Pura Gunung Lebah temple at the bottom of the ridge (free, dress respectfully with sarong). Spend time journaling or reading in the peaceful jungle surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class in Ubud — many budget options available from IDR 150,000–250,000 including a market visit, cooking 3–4 dishes, and eating your creations. Look for classes at Paon Bali, Casa Luna, or smaller local homestay kitchens for the most affordable options. Learn to make nasi goreng, satay, and Balinese sambal.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you cooked! If still hungry, visit a local warung. Stroll Ubud's streets in the evening — the town is beautifully lit and lively with art galleries, cafés, and live music at some venues.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit plate and coffee at the hotel or a nearby café — IDR 20,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepare during the cooking class — included in class fee
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a local warung or enjoy leftovers — IDR 25,000–40,000

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a mid-trip rest and culture day. The cooking class is one of Bali's most rewarding budget experiences — you learn skills you can use at home. Book the class the day before. Some classes include a morning market visit to buy fresh ingredients, which is an extra cultural bonus.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise hike at Mount Batur (active volcano, 1,717m). Depart from Ubud at 2–3 AM by pre-arranged transport (~IDR 50,000–100,000 each way). Guided sunrise trek with a local guide (compulsory, ~IDR 300,000–450,000 including guide, torch, and breakfast at the summit). Reach the summit at sunrise for breathtaking views over the crater lake and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend by mid-morning, soak tired feet in natural hot springs near the base of Batur (entry ~IDR 50,000–100,000). Return to Ubud by early afternoon. Rest at the hotel — you'll need it after the pre-dawn hike!
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening walk or light stretching/yoga to ease tired muscles. Treat yourself to a budget Balinese massage in Ubud (~IDR 80,000–120,000/hour) — there are dozens of affordable spas near the hotel. Early bedtime to recover.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast cooked at the volcano summit (included in guide package) — sunrise breakfast with a view!
meals.lunch: Warung near the hot springs or back in Ubud — nasi campur IDR 25,000–45,000
meals.dinner: Light meal at a local warung — soup or gado-gado IDR 25,000–40,000

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur hike is one of Bali's most iconic budget adventures. Book transport and guide the day before through your hotel or a local tour agency. Bring warm layers — the summit is cool at 3–4 AM. Wear sturdy shoes. The hike takes approximately 2 hours up and 1.5 hours down. This is a moderately challenging hike suitable for most fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in, do gentle stretching, and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the Neka Art Museum in Ubud (~IDR 75,000 entry) — one of Bali's finest art museums showcasing traditional and contemporary Balinese paintings across multiple pavilions set in beautiful gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip to Besakih Temple (Pura Besakih) — Bali's holiest and largest temple complex on the slopes of Mount Agung (~50 km from Ubud, shared transport IDR 50,000–100,000 each way). Entry ~IDR 60,000. Walk the extensive temple grounds and enjoy views of the sacred mountain. Return to Ubud by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a budget café in Ubud with a fresh coconut or Bali coffee. Browse the evening market stalls near Ubud Traditional Market for last-minute souvenirs or local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Full Balinese breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — nasi goreng with egg IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Warung near Besakih Temple — simple rice and vegetable dishes IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling or local rice restaurant in Ubud — IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: At Besakih, be aware of unofficial 'guides' who may approach you — you are not obligated to hire them. Dress very modestly (sarong and covered shoulders required). The temple complex is vast — wear comfortable shoes. The Neka Art Museum is a great way to understand Balinese art history before visiting temples.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the south — take a tourist shuttle to Uluwatu (~2.5 hrs from Ubud, IDR 80,000–120,000). Visit the spectacular Pura Luhur Uluwatu cliff temple (entry IDR 50,000) perched 70m above the Indian Ocean. Walk the cliff path with ocean views and watch for cheeky monkeys. Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Uluwatu, head to Padang Padang Beach (entry IDR 10,000–20,000) — a stunning small cove beach famous from the movie 'Eat Pray Love.' Swim in the crystal-clear water, relax on the white sand, and enjoy the beautiful scenery. Alternatively, visit Bingin Beach for a quieter option beloved by surfers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Uluwatu for the famous Kecak Fire Dance at sunset performed on a cliff-top stage overlooking the ocean (tickets IDR 100,000–150,000) — arguably the most dramatic setting for this performance in all of Bali. Take the shuttle back to Ubud afterward.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before early departure — fruit and bread IDR 15,000–25,000
meals.lunch: Warung near Padang Padang Beach — fresh grilled fish or nasi campur IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Eat before or after the Kecak show at a local warung near Uluwatu — IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the shuttle the day before. The Uluwatu Kecak Dance at sunset is one of Bali's most unforgettable experiences — highly recommended. Keep belongings secure around the Uluwatu temple monkeys. The beaches in Uluwatu area are among Bali's most beautiful — July conditions are typically excellent with calm, clear water.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class — try a different studio for variety. Radiantly Alive or The Yoga Barn in Ubud offer diverse styles (vinyasa, hatha, yin). Drop-in IDR 120,000–150,000. After class, visit the Ubud Traditional Market early morning (before 9 AM when it's most authentic and local) — buy fresh tropical fruits, snacks, and browse local produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or hire a driver and visit the scenic Jatiluwih Rice Terraces (~45 km from Ubud, UNESCO World Heritage Site, entry IDR 40,000). These terraces are less touristy than Tegallalang and far more expansive. Walk the 2 km trail through the paddies. Visit a traditional Balinese village nearby. Return to Ubud by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a special dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Ubud — Locavore To Go (budget-friendly sister of the famous Locavore) or Warung Pulau Kelapa for a memorable meal. Celebrate the near-end of your trip!

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or açaí bowl near the yoga studio — IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Warung at Jatiluwih — local set meal with rice terrace views IDR 35,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated budget dinner — Locavore To Go or similar IDR 80,000–150,000 for a special meal

day_by_day.notes: Jatiluwih is less visited than Tegallalang but far more impressive in scale. The drive there is also scenic through Balinese highland villages. If sharing a scooter rental, ensure both riders are comfortable. The Ubud market is best visited before 9 AM — after that it shifts to tourist goods. Bring a reusable bag.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach day — take a morning shuttle to Sanur Beach on Bali's east coast (~1 hr from Ubud, IDR 40,000–60,000). Sanur is calmer and less crowded than Kuta/Seminyak, with a lovely flat promenade along the shore. Swim in the calm, shallow water (Sanur is protected by a reef). Walk or rent a bicycle along the 5 km beachfront path (bike rental IDR 30,000–50,000/half day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sanur village — browse the beach market, visit local warungs, and relax under a palm tree. Optional: take a short boat trip to Nusa Lembongan island from Sanur pier (fast boat IDR 150,000–200,000 each way) for a few hours of snorkeling or beach time if budget allows. Return to Ubud by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Ubud — do some last-minute souvenir shopping at the Ubud Art Market. Enjoy a budget Balinese massage to relax before the journey home (~IDR 80,000–100,000/hour). Have a farewell dinner at your favorite warung discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before departure — coffee and banana pancakes IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a Sanur beach warung — grilled fish with rice IDR 45,000–75,000
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favorite local warung in Ubud — nasi campur or babi guling IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: Sanur is an underrated gem — calmer, cleaner, and more local-feeling than the busy south Bali tourist strips. The beachfront promenade is perfect for a leisurely morning. If doing the Nusa Lembongan day trip, depart from Sanur pier by 8–9 AM for maximum time. Pack light for this day — just beach essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the Campuhan Ridge Walk — a perfect bookend to the trip. Take photos, reflect on the journey, and soak in the peaceful jungle atmosphere one last time. Return to the hotel for a leisurely breakfast and begin packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout 11–12 PM). If flight is later in the day, store luggage at the hotel. Do any final souvenir shopping or café visits in Ubud. Head to the airport by Grab or pre-arranged taxi (~1.5–2 hrs from Ubud to Ngurah Rai Airport, IDR 200,000–300,000). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ngurah Rai International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, yoga, temples, rice terraces, and Balinese culture — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Full final breakfast at the hotel or a beloved local café — treat yourself to a proper nasi goreng IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Ubud before airport transfer or at the airport — IDR 30,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow 2–2.5 hours for the Ubud to airport transfer during peak hours — traffic around Kuta/Denpasar can be heavy. Confirm your flight departure time and check in online if possible. Use any remaining Indonesian Rupiah on snacks, last souvenirs, or airport food — currency is difficult to exchange outside Indonesia. Keep a small amount for airport taxi tip.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay (approximately 1.5–2 hours drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a gentle introductory stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk trail. The 9 km paved path winds through lush green hillsides and rice fields — perfect for a relaxed first afternoon. Enjoy the warm 25°C weather and panoramic valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Ubud town center (10-minute walk or short taxi ride). Explore Jalan Raya Ubud's evening market stalls and browse local handicrafts. Enjoy a quiet welcome dinner at a riverside warung.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Grab a light meal at the airport or a roadside warung on the drive to Ubud
meals.dinner: Murni's Warung — a beloved Ubud riverside restaurant with Indonesian classics; mid-range pricing, stunning gorge views

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm any yoga class bookings for the following morning. Exchange currency at a reputable money changer in Ubud rather than the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a 90-minute morning yoga class at the famous Yoga Barn in Ubud (a 15-minute walk from the hotel). Choose from Hatha, Vinyasa, or Yin classes — all beginner-friendly. Classes start at 07:00 and 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud — a lush nature reserve home to over 700 Balinese long-tailed macaques and ancient Hindu temples. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the forest paths. Afterward, browse the artisan galleries and boutiques along Monkey Forest Road.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud temple (performances usually begin at 19:30). This is a quintessential Balinese cultural experience not to be missed.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Kafe Ubud — fresh tropical fruit bowls, smoothies, and Balinese rice porridge (bubur)
meals.lunch: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — famous for Balinese suckling pig; affordable and authentic
meals.dinner: Locavore NXT — casual sister restaurant of Locavore, offering creative Indonesian cuisine at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Book Yoga Barn classes online in advance as morning sessions fill quickly. Kecak Dance tickets can be purchased at the venue (approx. IDR 100,000–150,000 per person).

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise walk along the Campuhan Ridge Walk starting at 06:00 to catch golden hour light over the valley. The trail is at its most magical and cool in the early morning. Return for breakfast by 08:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tegalalang Rice Terraces (approximately 20 minutes north of Ubud by scooter or taxi). Walk the terraced paths, learn about the traditional Subak irrigation system, and enjoy sweeping views. Optional: visit a nearby coffee plantation for a free luwak coffee tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Take a traditional Balinese cooking class in the late afternoon/evening (e.g., Paon Bali Cooking Class). Learn to prepare 5–7 traditional dishes using local ingredients sourced from a morning market visit.

meals.breakfast: Post-ridge walk breakfast at Karsa Kafe — perched above the Campuhan river with stunning views; avocado toast, smoothie bowls, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Warung at Tegalalang — simple local warungs near the rice terraces serve nasi campur and mie goreng at budget-friendly prices
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you cooked in the cooking class — typically included in the class package

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection for the rice terraces. Scooter rental (IDR 60,000–80,000/day) is the most convenient way to reach Tegalalang. Cooking class packages typically cost IDR 350,000–500,000 and include a market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin Yoga or meditation session at The Yoga Barn (07:00 class). Afterward, visit the Ubud Traditional Art Market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for handmade textiles, sarongs, wooden crafts, and souvenirs. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — the official residence of the Ubud royal family, featuring stunning Balinese architecture and manicured courtyards. Free entry. Then visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum, dedicated to the flamboyant Spanish-Balinese artist Antonio Blanco.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage and spa treatment at a reputable mid-range spa such as Taksu Spa or Bali Botanica Day Spa. Book a 90-minute full body massage with aromatherapy oils.

meals.breakfast: Seniman Coffee Studio — specialty Balinese single-origin coffee and artisan pastries; a local favorite
meals.lunch: Clear Café Ubud — healthy organic menu with vegan and vegetarian options; mid-range pricing
meals.dinner: Bridges Bali — elegant restaurant suspended over the Campuhan River gorge; Indonesian and international menu at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: The art market is best visited early morning before tour groups arrive. Spa treatments at quality mid-range spas cost approximately IDR 200,000–400,000 for 90 minutes. Book in advance for evening slots.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mount Batur for a sunrise trek (early start required — depart hotel at 02:00). Hike the active volcano (1,717m) with a licensed guide, reaching the summit by sunrise around 06:00. Enjoy panoramic views over Lake Batur and Mount Agung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Mount Batur and stop at Toya Devasya Natural Hot Springs on the shores of Lake Batur. Soak in the geothermal pools with views of the volcano — perfect recovery after the hike. Return to Ubud by 15:00.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery evening at the hotel. Gentle stretching or restorative yoga in your room. Early dinner and an early bedtime to recover from the pre-dawn start.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast provided by most trekking guides at the summit (usually banana, hard-boiled egg, and toast with Batur views)
meals.lunch: Lakeside warung near Toya Devasya — fresh grilled fish from Lake Batur, nasi goreng, and cold coconut water
meals.dinner: Warung Teges — a simple, authentic local warung near Campuhan; generous portions of Indonesian home cooking at very affordable prices

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable trekking guide in advance (IDR 300,000–500,000 per person including guide and breakfast). Bring warm layers for the summit — temperatures can drop to 10°C before sunrise. Toya Devasya entry fee is approximately IDR 150,000–200,000.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast followed by a gentle restorative yoga class at The Yoga Barn (09:00 session). Afterward, explore the quieter streets of Ubud's Penestanan neighborhood — known as the 'artists' village' with studios and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pura Tirta Empul — one of Bali's most sacred water temples, where locals and visitors participate in a traditional Hindu purification ritual (melukat) in the holy spring waters. Located 15 minutes from Ubud. Dress modestly and rent a sarong at the entrance.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Legong Dance performance at Puri Saren Agung (Ubud Palace) — one of Bali's most refined classical dance forms performed in the royal courtyard setting with torch lighting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Kafe at Campuhan — smoothie bowls, granola, and fresh papaya
meals.lunch: Warung Sopa — beloved local vegetarian restaurant with a beautiful garden setting; generous rice plates and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant — an Ubud institution for fine dining; creative French-Indonesian fusion using local ingredients. Treat yourself to the tasting menu for a special mid-trip celebration

day_by_day.notes: Tirta Empul requires a sarong and sash (available for rent at the entrance, IDR 15,000). If participating in the purification ritual, wear clothes you don't mind getting wet underneath. Legong Dance tickets at Ubud Palace cost approximately IDR 100,000.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — depart Ubud for the southern beach region. Check out of the boutique stay and transfer to Seminyak or Canggu (approximately 1.5 hours). En route, stop at the Garuda Wisnu Kencana (GWK) Cultural Park to see the magnificent 121-meter Garuda Wisnu Kencana statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the coast and check into a mid-range beach-area accommodation (or day-use option if staying mobile). Head straight to Seminyak Beach or Batu Bolong Beach (Canggu) for your first proper Bali beach afternoon. Rent a sun lounger, swim in the warm Indian Ocean, and soak up the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from Ku De Ta beach club (Seminyak) or La Brisa (Canggu) — both offer stunning sunset views with cocktails. Afterward, explore the vibrant Seminyak restaurant and bar strip.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Campuhan boutique stay before checkout
meals.lunch: Quick stop at a warung near GWK or grab lunch upon arrival at the coast — Nalu Bowls in Canggu for healthy acai and smoothie bowls
meals.dinner: Merah Putih Restaurant, Seminyak — stunning colonial-style space with modern Indonesian cuisine; mid-range to slightly upscale

day_by_day.notes: Book beach-area accommodation in advance for this portion of the trip. Seminyak and Canggu are the best mid-range beach bases. July is peak season so prices will be higher near the coast. GWK entry is approximately IDR 125,000 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach (many beach clubs and yoga studios in Canggu offer 06:30 outdoor sessions). Afterward, explore the Canggu neighborhood — browse the eclectic boutiques, surf shops, and café scene along Jalan Batu Bolong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson at Batu Bolong Beach or Echo Beach with a certified local instructor. The July swells are ideal for learning. Lessons typically last 2 hours and include board and rash vest rental.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Seminyak Square and Petitenget area for boutique shopping — Bali is famous for its fashion, homewares, and jewelry. Browse shops like Biasa, Bamboo Blonde, and local artisan stores.

meals.breakfast: Shelter Restaurant, Canggu — popular brunch spot with excellent eggs benedict, smoothie bowls, and Bali coffee
meals.lunch: Betelnut Café, Seminyak — casual café with fresh salads, sandwiches, and Indonesian dishes; great value
meals.dinner: Sarong Restaurant, Seminyak — sophisticated Asian-inspired sharing plates in a beautifully designed space; mid-range to upscale

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons cost approximately IDR 200,000–350,000 per person for a 2-hour group lesson. The July swell is consistent — ideal conditions for beginners. Wear reef-safe sunscreen as a courtesy to the ocean ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Bukit Peninsula — take a taxi or scooter south to explore the dramatic clifftop temples and beaches. Start with Pura Luhur Uluwatu, a stunning sea temple perched 70 meters above the Indian Ocean. Arrive early to avoid crowds and watch for cheeky monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Padang Padang Beach or Bingin Beach — two of Bali's most picturesque and secluded beaches tucked below limestone cliffs. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on the white sand. Both beaches have a small entry fee (IDR 10,000–15,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Uluwatu for the famous Kecak Fire Dance at sunset performed at the clifftop amphitheater — one of Bali's most dramatic performance settings with the ocean as a backdrop. Return to Seminyak/Canggu for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Organic, Seminyak — fresh organic juices, smoothie bowls, and healthy breakfast plates
meals.lunch: Single Fin Restaurant, Uluwatu — iconic clifftop restaurant above Suluban Beach with burgers, salads, and stunning views of surfers below
meals.dinner: Mama San Restaurant, Seminyak — vibrant Southeast Asian street food-inspired menu in a converted warehouse; great cocktails and mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong to enter Uluwatu Temple (available for rent at entrance). The Kecak Dance at Uluwatu starts at approximately 18:00 and tickets cost IDR 100,000–150,000. Book a reliable driver for the day (IDR 400,000–600,000) as the Bukit roads can be tricky on a scooter.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach yoga session at sunrise on Seminyak Beach — many local instructors offer open-air sessions on the sand. Afterward, visit the Seminyak Beach area and walk north along the uninterrupted stretch of beach toward Petitenget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most photographed sea temples, built on a rocky islet offshore. Accessible at low tide. The surrounding area has craft markets and beautiful coastal views. Located approximately 20 minutes from Seminyak.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a sunset cocktail at Tanah Lot before returning to Seminyak. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a beachfront restaurant watching the last light fade over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: La Lucciola, Seminyak — beachfront Italian-Indonesian restaurant; excellent breakfast with ocean views
meals.lunch: Local warung near Tanah Lot — nasi campur, satay, and fresh coconut; very affordable
meals.dinner: Barbacoa, Seminyak — Argentine-style BBQ with Balinese influences; excellent grilled meats and fresh seafood at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times for Tanah Lot — the temple is most accessible and photogenic at low tide. Entry fee is approximately IDR 60,000 per person. The site is crowded at sunset so arrive by 16:30 for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to East Bali — depart early for a day trip to the Sidemen Valley and Tirtagangga Water Palace. The drive east (approximately 2–2.5 hours) passes through stunning volcanic landscapes and traditional villages. Tirtagangga features ornate tiered fountains and pools you can swim in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Candidasa coast or Virgin Beach (Pantai Perasi) — a hidden gem with calm turquoise waters, far fewer crowds than the west coast, and excellent snorkeling on the reef. Spend 2 hours swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Seminyak/Canggu, stopping for dinner in Klungkung or Gianyar. Arrive back at the hotel by 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Warung at Tirtagangga — simple local food with views of the water palace gardens; fresh fish and rice dishes
meals.dinner: Warung Mak Beng, if passing through Sanur on the return — legendary Balinese fried fish institution that has been operating since 1941; incredibly affordable and delicious

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for this day trip (IDR 500,000–700,000 for the full day) as it covers significant distance. Tirtagangga entry and swimming fee is approximately IDR 50,000–75,000. Bring snorkeling gear or rent locally at Virgin Beach.

day_by_day.morning: Final dedicated yoga session — book a 2-hour workshop or masterclass at a reputable studio (Canggu has excellent options like The Practice or Desa Seni). Focus on deepening your practice and integrating the mindfulness of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach afternoon — return to your favorite beach spot for a final swim and sun session. Alternatively, try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) at Seminyak Beach (rentals available, IDR 100,000–150,000/hour). Pick up any last-minute gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — choose a special restaurant to celebrate the end of a wonderful trip. Consider a beachfront table at sunset for a memorable final evening in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Revolver Espresso, Seminyak — Bali's best specialty coffee with excellent breakfast sandwiches and pastries
meals.lunch: Sea Circus, Seminyak — colorful, fun café with Mexican-inspired dishes, fresh salads, and excellent cocktails
meals.dinner: Métis Restaurant, Seminyak — elegant French-Mediterranean cuisine in a stunning colonial villa setting; perfect for a special farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to pack and prepare for departure. Confirm your airport transfer for the following day. Check airline baggage allowances if you've purchased crafts or souvenirs. Leave a review for your Ubud boutique stay!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — enjoy a slow breakfast and a last walk along the beach or neighborhood streets. Depending on your flight time, visit a nearby café for a final Balinese coffee. Check out of accommodation and arrange transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (allow 1.5–2 hours from Seminyak in July traffic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure — arrive at least 2.5 hours before international flights. Browse duty-free for last-minute Balinese coffee, chocolate, or Arak (local spirit) to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — carry the memories of 13 days of beaches, yoga, temples, and incredible Balinese culture.

meals.breakfast: Nook Bali, Seminyak — charming café in a rice field setting; smoothie bowls, eggs, and Bali coffee for a perfect final breakfast
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or grab a final nasi goreng at a warung near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: July is peak season — allow extra time for airport traffic, especially between 10:00–14:00. Ngurah Rai Airport has good dining and shopping options if you arrive early. Declare any wooden or plant-based items at customs when returning home. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — private luxury transfer arranged to Campuhan Ridge Walk, Ubud Boutique Stay. Settle into your villa, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink and fruit platter prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk trail directly from the hotel — a 2 km scenic ridge path through lush green hills and river valleys. Perfect for unwinding after the flight. Light stretching and breathing exercises at a scenic viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private villa terrace overlooking the jungle canopy. Ease into the Bali rhythm with a traditional Balinese welcome massage at the hotel spa (60 minutes).

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel — tropical fruit, cold-pressed juices, and Indonesian rice dishes served upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bridges Bali Restaurant, perched above the Campuhan River gorge — order the pan-seared barramundi and finish with a dark chocolate lava cake. Exceptional wine list available.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — focus on acclimatization. Ensure your villa butler has your dietary preferences for the rest of the stay. The Campuhan Ridge Walk is best done in the late afternoon light (16:00–18:00) to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session at 06:30 on the hotel's open-air yoga pavilion overlooking the Campuhan valley — guided by a certified Balinese yoga instructor. Follow with a 90-minute Balinese herbal scrub and flower bath at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud — explore ancient Hindu temples and lush forest pathways. Then visit the Ubud Art Market for curated premium handicrafts, hand-woven textiles, and silver jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud temple (begins at 19:30) — one of Bali's most mesmerizing cultural spectacles performed under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet in-villa breakfast — freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit platter, Balinese black rice pudding with coconut cream, and cold-pressed green juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Locavore NXT, Ubud — Bali's premier farm-to-table experience; try the seasonal tasting menu with local produce pairings
meals.dinner: Post-performance dinner at Mozaic Restaurant Ubud — award-winning French-Indonesian fusion; book the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing in advance

day_by_day.notes: Book Kecak Dance tickets in advance through your hotel concierge. Mozaic requires advance reservations — ideally booked before arrival. Bring a light shawl for the evening temple visit.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and meditation session at Tirta Empul Temple — a sacred water purification temple. Experience the traditional melukat (holy water purification ritual) with a private priest guide. Deeply spiritual and rejuvenating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tegallalang Rice Terraces — one of UNESCO's most celebrated cultural landscapes. Private guided walk through the cascading emerald terraces. Stop at a premium café perched above the terraces for a cold-pressed juice break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private couples' or solo Balinese Boreh body treatment (traditional warming spice wrap) followed by a 4-hand massage at the spa.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel — banana pancakes, fresh papaya, and Balinese coffee before departure to the temple
meals.lunch: Alfresco lunch at Swept Away at COMO Shambhala Estate — organic Balinese cuisine served beside the Wos River; try the grilled snapper with sambal matah
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner arranged by the hotel butler in your villa garden — a bespoke 5-course Indonesian menu with a sommelier-selected wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for Tirta Empul (sarong and sash provided). Melukat ritual should be done respectfully — photography is limited inside the bathing pools. Tegallalang is best visited before 10:00 or after 15:00 to avoid tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin yoga and pranayama (breathwork) class at a premium yoga studio in central Ubud — The Yoga Barn offers world-class instructors. 90-minute restorative session followed by a green smoothie bowl at the studio café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private silver jewelry-making workshop with a master Balinese artisan in Celuk village — craft your own bespoke keepsake piece. Followed by a visit to the Blanco Renaissance Museum — the flamboyant home and gallery of Spanish-Balinese artist Antonio Blanco.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at Karsa Kafe, a hidden gem above the Campuhan River, then stroll back along the ridge walk under the early evening sky.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed watermelon juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Naughty Nuri's Warung (iconic Ubud institution) — BBQ pork ribs, satay, and legendary martinis in a casual but celebrated setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Room4Dessert by Will Goldfarb — a world-renowned dessert-focused tasting experience; pair with natural wines for a unique and memorable evening

day_by_day.notes: Room4Dessert is one of the world's top dessert restaurants — reservations are essential and fill up weeks in advance. The silver workshop takes approximately 2–3 hours; confirm timing with your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hike to the summit of Mount Batur (1,717 m) — depart at 03:30 for a 2-hour guided ascent to witness one of Southeast Asia's most spectacular sunrises above the clouds. Cook eggs in volcanic steam vents at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and soak in natural volcanic hot springs at Toya Devasya Hot Springs on the shores of Lake Batur — private pool access available. Enjoy a light recovery massage poolside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud by 17:00. Relax with a restorative yoga nidra session at the hotel before a peaceful evening.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy pack prepared by the hotel — energy bars, bananas, trail mix, and a thermos of Balinese coffee; full breakfast served on return
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Toya Devasya — grilled corn, fresh fruit, and Balinese babi guling (suckling pig) served with a view of the caldera lake
meals.dinner: Quiet in-hotel dinner — light and nourishing post-hike meal; opt for the hotel's Balinese curry with steamed rice and fresh coconut water

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur hike requires a certified guide (arranged through the hotel). Wear layers — the summit is cold before sunrise. This is a physically demanding day; ensure you are well-rested the night before. Toya Devasya private pools can be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — gentle 60-minute Hatha yoga session on your villa terrace at 07:00. Followed by a luxurious 2-hour Balinese Jamu wellness ritual at the hotel spa (herbal compress, full-body oil massage, and facial).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and surrounding streets — browse premium galleries showcasing traditional and contemporary Balinese art. Visit the Seniwati Gallery, dedicated exclusively to Balinese women artists.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional Balinese cooking class hosted at a local chef's family compound — learn to prepare 5 authentic dishes using fresh market ingredients harvested that morning.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-villa breakfast — nasi goreng (Balinese fried rice), fresh tropical fruit, coconut yogurt parfait, and freshly brewed Kintamani single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hujan Locale — modern Indonesian cuisine celebrating regional archipelago flavors; try the braised short rib rendang with fermented cassava
meals.dinner: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — a private sit-down dinner of the dishes you prepared, served in the chef's family compound garden with rice wine

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically run 3–4 hours including the market visit. Confirm with your concierge whether the class includes a morning market tour (recommended). Gallery visits are free or low-cost.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Seminyak/Canggu coastal area (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into a luxury beach club day pass at Potato Head Beach Club or Finns Beach Club — sun loungers, private cabana, and beachside service included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Surf lesson with a private instructor at Batu Bolong Beach, Canggu — one of Bali's most iconic surf breaks, suitable for beginners and intermediates. Followed by a beachside stretch and cool-down session.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at La Brisa Beach Club, Canggu — a stunning driftwood-constructed venue on the beach. Watch the famous Bali sunset over the Indian Ocean with a signature cocktail in hand.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — fresh açaí bowl, granola, and cold-brew coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Potato Head Beach Club — wood-fired pizzas, ceviche, and tropical cocktails with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sarong Restaurant, Seminyak — one of Bali's most celebrated fine dining venues; Asian-inspired tasting menu in a stunning colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: This is a beach and surf day — pack sunscreen SPF 50+, rash guard, and reef-safe products. Private surf instructors can be arranged through La Brisa or local surf schools. Return transfer to Ubud departs at 20:30.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Vinyasa flow yoga class at The Yoga Barn (07:00) — energizing flow session. Afterward, visit the Ubud Traditional Market at its freshest hour (06:00–08:00) for a sensory exploration of local spices, flowers, and offerings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour to Pura Besakih — Bali's holiest and most magnificent temple complex on the slopes of Mount Agung. Known as the 'Mother Temple,' it consists of 23 separate temples. Private guide ensures respectful and insightful access.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Twilight meditation session at the hotel's garden pavilion guided by a resident Balinese healer — a deeply calming experience connecting with Balinese spiritual traditions.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga snack — banana and almond butter; full breakfast after the market visit at a local warung serving fresh jajan pasar (traditional Balinese sweets) and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch prepared by the hotel for the Besakih journey — sandwiches, fruit, and cold-pressed juice enjoyed at a scenic mountain viewpoint
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alaya Resort Ubud's Plantation Restaurant — refined Indonesian cuisine with stunning rice terrace views; try the slow-roasted duck betutu

day_by_day.notes: Besakih requires modest dress (sarong and sash mandatory — available at the temple). A private guide is strongly recommended to navigate the complex and avoid aggressive unofficial guides. The round trip takes approximately 4–5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Nusa Penida island — depart from Sanur Harbor by speedboat (45 minutes). Visit the iconic Kelingking Beach (T-Rex cliff viewpoint) — one of the most photographed landscapes in all of Indonesia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling excursion at Crystal Bay — pristine coral reefs, tropical fish, and the possibility of spotting Mola Mola (ocean sunfish, in season July–October). Private boat and guide included. Visit the natural infinity pool at Broken Beach (Pasih Uug).
day_by_day.evening: Return speedboat to Sanur by 17:30, private transfer back to Ubud. Arrive hotel by 19:30 for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict, tropical fruit, and Balinese coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside warung on Nusa Penida — grilled lobster, prawns, and local sambal with coconut rice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Watercress Ubud — a romantic riverside restaurant with a creative menu blending Balinese and international flavors; excellent cocktail program

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Penida roads are rough — a private 4WD with driver is essential on the island. The Kelingking descent to the beach is extremely steep and optional. Bring motion sickness medication if prone to seasickness on the speedboat crossing.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Ashtanga yoga practice with a senior teacher at a boutique Ubud studio (06:30). Afterward, visit a traditional Balinese healer (Balian) for a wellness consultation and energy healing session — a profound and authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private batik and natural dyeing workshop at a traditional Ubud textile studio — create your own hand-dyed fabric piece using ancient Balinese techniques. Visit the Threads of Life textile gallery showcasing rare ceremonial textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-Ubud sunset walk along the Campuhan Ridge — the full 5 km loop at golden hour. Return for a luxurious evening at the hotel spa with a signature 3-hour 'Bali Ritual' treatment.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie bowl at the studio; full brunch back at the hotel — eggs royale, freshly baked pastries, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Clear Café Ubud — organic, plant-based, and raw food menu; try the rainbow bowl and raw chocolate dessert
meals.dinner: Special dinner at Ku De Ta's sister property or Merah Putih Restaurant, Seminyak (if willing to travel) — or opt for a private chef dinner at the villa arranged by the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Balian healers are deeply respected in Balinese culture — approach the session with openness and respect. Your hotel concierge can recommend reputable healers. The textile workshop produces a keepsake to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day transfer to Uluwatu Peninsula on Bali's southern tip. Morning beach time at Padang Padang Beach — a stunning cove featured in 'Eat Pray Love.' Swim in crystal-clear waters and relax on white sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cliff-top exploration at Uluwatu Temple (Pura Luhur Uluwatu) — one of Bali's six key spiritual temples perched 70 meters above the crashing Indian Ocean. Private guide explains the temple's significance in Balinese Hinduism.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset (18:00) — performed on a clifftop stage with the ocean as a backdrop, this is considered the most spectacular setting for the performance in all of Bali.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — smoothie, avocado toast, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Single Fin Uluwatu — a legendary surf bar and restaurant perched above Uluwatu's famous left-hand break; order the fish tacos and watch surfers below
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sundays Beach Club or Omnia Dayclub's restaurant — upscale dining with dramatic clifftop ocean views; grilled seafood platter and premium wine

day_by_day.notes: Beware of monkeys at Uluwatu Temple — secure sunglasses, phones, and jewelry. Sarong required at the temple. Book Kecak Dance tickets in advance. This is a full-day excursion — return to Ubud late evening or consider overnight at a Uluwatu luxury property.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga session on the Campuhan Ridge Walk — a private outdoor session with your instructor at the most scenic point of the trail (06:00). A perfect mindful farewell to Ubud's natural beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure time at the hotel — final swim, lounge in the villa, and enjoy the hotel's amenities. Optional: a private Balinese painting class with a local artist in the hotel garden (2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner experience — reserve the chef's table at Locavore, Ubud's internationally acclaimed restaurant (ranked among Asia's 50 Best Restaurants). Full tasting menu with beverage pairing.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory in-villa breakfast — a spread of all your favorite dishes from the trip, curated by the hotel chef with fresh local produce
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel pool — mezze-style sharing plates, cold-pressed juices, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Locavore Ubud — 8-course tasting menu celebrating Indonesian biodiversity; wine, sake, or juice pairing available. One of Bali's most memorable dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Locavore reservations must be made weeks in advance — ensure your concierge books this on Day 1 of your trip. Pack any purchased souvenirs and artworks carefully. Confirm your departure transfer for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — gentle stretching and meditation in the villa garden at sunrise. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast. Last walk through the hotel grounds to absorb the sounds and scents of the Campuhan valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow 2.5 hours for the journey from Ubud. Enjoy complimentary access to the Bali Lounge (Garuda Indonesia Premier Lounge or similar) for pre-departure relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry the serenity, wellness, and beauty of the island with you.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a curated Balinese feast: nasi campur, fresh tropical fruit, Balinese coffee, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport lounge — finger sandwiches, fruit, and refreshments
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 12:00 — arrange a late checkout if your flight is in the afternoon to maximize your final morning. Tip your villa butler, driver, and regular service staff generously as a gesture of gratitude for the exceptional service. Ensure you have any required customs documentation for items purchased (textiles, art, jewelry).

query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA
